question: How do I get my criminal record sealed or expunged, how long do I have to wait, and what does it cost?

groups: without being charged with the commission of a crime
waive any court fees and costs
after a disposition of the charge

gold_sections.why: A person arrested or confined on or after October 1, 2007 and released without being charged is entitled to expungement of all police records; the law enforcement unit must expunge within 60 days of release and notify the Central Repository, which has 60 days; no fee or costs; a remedy if they fail.

Automatic expungement, 3 years after disposition, of records of a charge (a crime or a civil cannabis offense, other than a non-appearance Transportation violation) where no charge in the case ended other than in acquittal, dismissal, not guilty or a non-treatment nolle prosequi; the court sends notice of the date.

After an acquittal, dismissal, not guilty or non-treatment nolle prosequi the court must notify the defendant (by mail if absent) of the right to petition for expungement under § 10-105 (missing from the downloaded text), with a written form for a general waiver and release of tort claims.

Cost rules for expungement under Title 10, Subtitle 1: unpaid court fees or costs are not a bar, and the court waives court fees and costs tied to the expunged charge (shielding, Subtitle 3, is not covered).

Petition to shield shieldable convictions: no earlier than 3 years after the whole sentence is satisfied, new-conviction and pending-case bars, unit rule, service on the State's Attorney with 30 days to object, discretionary grant if unopposed, hearing on objection, good cause, victim notice, one grant per lifetime.

Defines 'shield' (records made inaccessible to the public) and the twelve shieldable convictions (disorderly conduct, disturbing the peace, CDS possession, trespass, driving without a license, and others).

In the version in force since January 31, 2026, Maryland Judiciary Case Search may not show charges ending in acquittal, dismissal or any nolle prosequi, stets marked at least 3 years earlier, or pardoned cannabis-possession convictions; automatic, no petition.
DPSCS had to remove from the Central Repository, by July 1, 2024 and without a petition, every case whose only charge was cannabis possession issued before July 1, 2023.
Case Search may not show a case whose only charge was cannabis possession disposed of before July 1, 2023.
After a nolle prosequi of all charges against a defendant never served, the District Court may order expungement without a petition unless the State objects and shows cause, and may not assess costs.

Shielding never applies to a domestically related crime, and shielded records stay fully accessible to criminal justice units, employers and licensing agencies with a statutory duty or authorization to check, and others listed.
Case Search may not refer to the existence of shielded records.

Effect of shielding: those with access may not pass shielded information on, and employers, schools and State or local units may not require disclosure of shielded charges or refuse a person solely for not disclosing them.
Unit rule: charges from the same incident are a unit, and if one charge or conviction in the unit cannot be expunged, none of them can (minor traffic and cannabis possession charges excepted).

When all charges end in acquittal, dismissal, probation before judgment, nolle prosequi or stet, the court must advise the defendant that the records and DNA may be expunged under Title 10, Subtitle 1 and Public Safety Title 2, Subtitle 5.
Effect of expungement: employers, schools and licensing units may not require disclosure of expunged charges or refuse a person solely for not disclosing them.

Older route for arrests before October 1, 2007 without charge: written request to the law enforcement unit within 8 years of the incident, 60-day handling, District Court application within 30 days of a denial, no fee.

Scope: police and court records are subject to expungement, including records from before July 1, 1975 (whose § 10-105 limitation periods run from entitlement); minor traffic violations, investigatory files and court opinions are excluded.

nuggets.text: Shielding makes the court and police records of a conviction inaccessible to the public, and it is available only for twelve listed minor convictions, such as disorderly conduct, disturbing the peace, failure to obey a lawful order, lesser malicious destruction of property, trespass on posted property, CDS or noncontrolled substance possession, paraphernalia, driving without a license or while suspended or uninsured, and prostitution.

answer: Arrested on or after October 1, 2007 and released without charge? You are entitled to expungement of police records [N1]; police must do it within 60 days without a request [N2], free [N3]. If every charge ended in acquittal, dismissal, not guilty or a nolle prosequi not requiring treatment, the records are expunged automatically 3 years after disposition [N4]. The court must also notify you of your right to petition under section 10-105, with a tort-claims waiver form [N5]; its timing rules are not in this text. Probation before judgment or stet may also be expungeable [N6]. Case Search automatically hides acquittals, dismissals, nolle prosequi, and stets after 3 years [N11]; cannabis-only possession cases charged before July 1, 2023 were to be expunged without a petition [N12]. Unpaid court fees cannot block expungement, and the court waives the expunged charge's fees and costs [N7][N8], but not for shielding; no statute here sets a petition fee. Twelve minor convictions, such as disorderly conduct, trespass or drug possession, can be shielded from public view [N13], but not domestically related crimes [N14]. Petition no earlier than 3 years after finishing your whole sentence, including probation or parole [N15]; a new conviction blocks it unless that conviction itself becomes eligible; so does a pending case [N16]. The State's Attorney has 30 days to object; otherwise the court may grant it [N17]. One grant per lifetime [N18]; police and some employers still see shielded records [N19]. Employers cannot demand expunged or shielded charges [N20][N21].

gaps: The general petition for expungement (Criminal Procedure § 10-105, to which § 10-105.2 points after acquittal, dismissal, not guilty or nolle prosequi and § 6-232 after probation before judgment or stet, with the limitation periods § 10-102(b)(3) mentions and the general waiver and release of tort claims sent with the § 10-105.2 notice), pardoned convictions (§ 10-106), convictions (§ 10-110) and the definitions (§ 10-101) are missing from the downloaded text, so the main petition path is not modeled.

Arrests or confinements before October 1, 2007 without a charge (§ 10-103) required a written request to the law enforcement unit within 8 years of the incident, a window that has closed for every such incident; that route is not modeled.

The shielding petition's form, any filing fee and where to file within the county come from the Maryland Rules and court cost schedules, not the statutes; the § 10-105.4 fee waiver covers expungement under Subtitle 1, not shielding.

The 3-year automatic expungement under § 10-105.1 is a scheduled event, modeled as a 3-year clock on the custodians' step; the two court notices (§ 10-105.1(b) to the custodians and § 10-105.2 to the defendant) have no statutory order and are modeled as parallel; no remedy for a missed date is stated.

§ 10-303(f) sets no time for the victim notice; it is placed right after filing, before service on the State's Attorney, only so the shielding path stays one sequence; the 30-day objection clock runs from service (§ 10-303(d)(2)).
Whether the § 10-303(e)(3) good-cause power can overcome the eligibility bars is not stated; the tables apply the bars first.

Automatic relief without any step by the person is not modeled as steps: Case Search removal of acquittals, dismissals, nolle prosequi and stets at least 3 years old (§ 10-401) and of cannabis-only possession cases (§ 10-111), and DPSCS expungement of cannabis-only possession cases charged before July 1, 2023 (§ 10-112); nor are the District Court's no-petition, no-cost expungement after a nolle prosequi against an unserved defendant (§ 10-104), juvenile records (Courts § 3-8A-27.1), DNA records (Public Safety § 2-511) and vacatur for trafficking victims (§ 8-302).

version_flags: Criminal Procedure § 10-401: the version that took effect January 31, 2026 (Chapter 95 of 2025) is in force on 2026-10-10. Compared with the superseded 'IN EFFECT' text printed with it, it drops the exception for a nolle prosequi with a requirement of drug or alcohol treatment (so every nolle prosequi is now kept off Case Search), and adds stets marked at least 3 years earlier and pardoned cannabis-possession convictions. Automatic expungement under § 10-105.1 and the § 10-105.2 notice still exclude treatment nolle prosequi, so the two rules now differ.
Criminal Procedure § 10-112: the DPSCS deadline (on or before July 1, 2024) has passed; the section still describes which cannabis-only cases were to be removed from the Central Repository.
notes: Maryland statutes only, as downloaded (open-us-law). Criminal Procedure §§ 10-101, 10-105, 10-106 and 10-110, the core petition sections for non-conviction dispositions, PBJ, stet, pardons and convictions (with their waiting periods), are missing from the download although other sections cite §§ 10-101 and 10-105 (§§ 10-105.2, 10-102(b)(3), 10-301, 10-305) and § 6-232 points to Title 10, Subtitle 1; hence coverage is partial and the answer relies on the sections present. No filing fee amount appears in any downloaded section. § 10-103 (pre-October 1, 2007 arrests without charge) is a supporting section only: its 8-year request window has run for every such incident. Related routes not in the nuggets: § 10-108 (expunged records may be opened only by court order; violation is a misdemeanor); General Provisions § 4-327 (custodians must deny inspection of shielded records except to those listed in § 10-302(b));§ 10-105.3 (cannabis possession resentencing); Courts § 3-8A-27.1 (juvenile records: petition at age 18 and 2 years after the last official action, with conditions); Public Safety § 2-511 (DNA samples and records destroyed and expunged automatically within 60 days of a non-conviction, but not when the case is put on the stet docket or the person receives probation before judgment, so the § 6-232 advice is only that DNA records may be expungeable); § 8-302 (vacating listed convictions of trafficking victims); Commercial Law § 14-1324 (once a record has been expunged, shielded or the judgment vacated, a mugshot website must remove the photo free of charge within 30 days after receiving a request by certified mail or e-mail); Transportation § 16-117.1 (MVA expunges public driving records, not criminal records). Protective-order and peace-order shielding (Family Law § 4-512, Courts § 3-1510) concern civil records and are excluded.
